newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher on yen's plunge.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher on yen's plunge.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher across the board on Tuesday, due to the yen's plunge against the dollar and the Chicago market's gains overnight, traders said.
Prices were 320 to 490 yen higher, with the benchmark March 1998 contract up 320 yen at 16,370 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 56,816 lots.

"Active buying by local investors continued throughout the day. We're watching to see if the yen will fall further," a brokerage trader said. The dollar surged to above 126.00 yen by late afternoon, against around 124.70 yen on Monday afternoon.
The spot May corn contract on CBOT Project A was trading at $3.01-1/4 per bushel at 0855 GMT, against $3.00-3/4 at Monday's close.
Spot May CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system were at $8.61 per bushel, against $8.62-3/4 at Monday's close.
